skill.name: sound-effects
skill.description: Add recorded sound effects and licensed music to motion-graphics videos. Check beat alignment, measure exported loudness, and generate cue reports for human review.
skill.summary: Build a measured sound pass with recorded effects, beat checks, loudness measurements, and an interactive swap report.
skill.author: barty-bart

security_audit.summary: Reviewed all 400 supplied findings; most are benign documentation, attribution metadata, JSON escaping, and authorized media operations. Predictable temporary files are confirmed risks; unchecked eval remains conservatively confirmed without demonstrated media-only code injection. No evidence found of prompt injection or exfiltration; 77 omitted static matches still require manual review before automatic publication. Static review was capped at 400/477 representative findings; omitted static matches are unconfirmed, so automatic publishing stays disabled until manual review.

remediation.suggestion: Manually review the omitted 77 static analyzer matches or reduce bundled generated/vendor/reference content before enabling automatic publication.

remediation.issue: Frame-rate parsing evaluates unchecked ffprobe output as Python.
remediation.suggestion: Replace eval with fractions.Fraction or explicit numerator and denominator parsing. Check tool success and require a finite positive frame rate.

remediation.issue: Shared predictable temporary audio and frame files allow collisions, substitution, and possible disclosure.
remediation.suggestion: Use a private tempfile.TemporaryDirectory for each run, place all intermediate files there, and clean up reliably after success or failure.

remediation.issue: The static finding catalog omitted 77 matches from adjudication.
remediation.suggestion: Have a reviewer adjudicate the remaining matches before automatic publication. Do not treat the 400 supplied verdicts as complete static coverage.

high_findings.title: Dynamic code evaluation with eval()
high_findings.confidence_reasoning: eval executes unchecked ffprobe output as Python instead of parsing a frame-rate ratio. Normal output is numeric; no media-only injection was demonstrated, so this remains conservatively confirmed.

medium_findings.title: Temp directory access
medium_findings.confidence_reasoning: FFmpeg overwrites a predictable shared temporary audio filename without private allocation or cleanup. Concurrent runs can corrupt results; permissive temporary-file access can expose extracted audio.

medium_findings.title: Temp directory access
medium_findings.confidence_reasoning: Cue frames use predictable shared temporary filenames with overwrite enabled. Concurrent runs or preexisting links can redirect or corrupt writes where filesystem protections permit.

medium_findings.title: Temp directory access
medium_findings.confidence_reasoning: The report reads cue frames from predictable shared temporary names without verifying ownership or isolation. Another run or local process can substitute frames and invalidate review evidence.

content.user_title: Add Measured Sound Effects to Motion Graphics
content.value_statement: Motion-graphics videos need synchronized sound effects and consistent audio levels. This skill combines recorded effects, beat checks, exported loudness measurements, and reports for human review.
actual_capabilities: Guide cue-list creation from animation timelines or detected scene cuts and map cue types to recorded sound categories.
Compare detected beats with low-frequency kick transients and search music offsets that reduce cut-to-beat timing errors.
Place recorded effects from a default kit or alternatives, with runtime downloads for selected Mixkit sounds.
Export an MP4 and iteratively adjust gain and limiting toward -16 LUFS and true peaks below -4 dBFS.
Generate beat plots, cue frames, waveform checks, credits, license warnings, and up to five listening timestamps.
Create an HTML report with sound previews and alternative selections that export a swap file for another run.
limitations: Requires Python 3.10+, FFmpeg, curl for runtime downloads, and the documented Python audio and plotting libraries.
Bundled sounds are compressed previews; runtime downloads and current license checks require network access.
The script replaces original video audio and does not implement the documented voiceover ducking workflow.
Music must exceed the video duration; beat detection and ten export attempts do not guarantee timing or loudness targets.

use_cases.title: Score a Product Demo
use_cases.description: Add clicks, appearances, transitions, and reveals to an existing product animation, then inspect cue timing and measured audio levels.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Social Video
use_cases.description: Select recorded effects and music for a social video, verify publication permissions, and generate source credits.

use_cases.title: Review a Client Sound Pass
use_cases.description: Compare sound alternatives in an HTML report, export selections, and rerun the mix with stable cue indices.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a First Sound Pass
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my silent motion-graphics video and propose a cue list using the default sound kit. Ask about music licensing and publication before exporting.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: plan cues for an existing silent video.

prompt_templates.title: Mix a Supplied Track
prompt_templates.prompt: Add sound effects to this silent video using my licensed music track. Check beat alignment, measure exported loudness, and provide listening timestamps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: create a measured mix with user-supplied music.

prompt_templates.title: Revise Sound Choices
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply my exported swap selections to the previous sound pass. Keep cue indices stable, regenerate the report, and recheck loudness and credits.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: revise a completed mix through the swap report.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Final Sound Pass
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this sound pass for a client release using only sounds whose licenses allow the publication use case. Report timing errors, exported loudness, mono measurements, and unresolved issues.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert: review measured results and publication permissions.

output_examples.input: Plan sound effects for a silent product demo before choosing music.
output: Proposed cues: a quiet click for the button, a pop for the card, and an impact for the final reveal.
Music selection and publication use case remain unconfirmed.
No audio quality or loudness result is claimed before rendering and measurement.

output_examples.input: Describe the deliverables from a completed sound pass.
output: Video with mixed audio, an interactive cue report, and a beat-grid plot.
Cue frames and waveform checks, a measurement log, and up to five timestamps for headphone review.
A credits list with music details and warnings for unconfirmed licenses.

output_examples.input: Replace an effect selected in the HTML report.
output: The report exports selected alternatives into a swap file.
A new run applies those selections, rebuilds the video, and updates measurements and credits.

best_practices: Confirm the publication use case and current source licenses before exporting the final video.
Inspect exported MP4 measurements and cue plots, then listen to the suggested timestamps with headphones.
Use trusted manifests and media in an isolated workspace; avoid concurrent runs until temporary-file handling is fixed.
anti_patterns: Treating beat plots or loudness measurements as proof that a mix sounds good.
Running the script on a video with essential original audio without a separate preservation plan.
Committing runtime Mixkit downloads or assuming every listed license permits every distribution format.

faq.question: What software does this skill require?
faq.answer: It requires Python 3.10+, FFmpeg, librosa, soundfile, numpy, scipy, and matplotlib. Runtime downloads also use curl.

faq.question: Does it generate synthetic sounds or music?
faq.answer: No. It uses recorded sound files and a supplied or selected music track.

faq.question: Can it work without an internet connection?
faq.answer: Local mixing can use bundled sounds and local music. Default typing, other runtime sounds, and current license checks require network access.

faq.question: Are all sounds licensed for every use?
faq.answer: No. Bundled sounds are listed as CC0, while runtime Mixkit assets have restrictions. Confirm current terms for your publication use case.

faq.question: Does the script preserve existing voiceover?
faq.answer: No. It maps video from the source and audio from the new mix. Preserve voiceover separately before using the script.

faq.question: Does it guarantee professional audio quality?
faq.answer: No. It targets measurable loudness and timing goals but still requires human listening. Review final measurements because export attempts are limited.
